doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Drummers, the sad early Basie band, and a lost battle with Glen Gray
summary: After Gus Johnson fell ill, Wess and Basie found Sonny Payne; the early band was weak against Ellington at the Band Box.

bands.name: Glen Gray and the Casa Loma Orchestra

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Who were some of your favorite drummers and bass players during that period?
Oh, Kenny Clarke. Now you mean with Basie band?

Well there were only two, Gus Johnson and Gus Johnson got sick so we were trying out different drummers, and they didn’t make it. He even called Papa Jo back, but Papa Jo didn’t fit with that band you know, it was a different thing. So one day he says, “hey Magic, come over, I got a little drummer down here, let’s go catch him.” So we went down to the Regal Theater in Chicago, me and Bas’, and Sonny Payne was there with I think maybe Erskine Hawkins or somebody. And he say, “What you think, man?” I say, “Yeah, he can make it.” So eventually he got Sonny and Joe Williams came in at the same time you know. So that’s when, the band really started to get together you know. Before that I mean when I joined the band, I thought, I said, this is the saddest band I’ve ever played with in my life. Well it was the situation you know that we were in. We had to do two weeks in the Band Box, opposite Duke Ellington. And you know what I mean.

That ain’t no competition, we were out of the park, we weren’t even in it. We used to listen, Benny Powell and I used to listen to tapes from that band, boy we’d listen to those tapes and laugh, ‘cause the band was so sad it was funny, you know. And Duke was fired up. But we had a lot of spirit, but that was all. The band was just sad that’s all. That was funny. Another time I was really embarrassed. I was working with this dance hall band and I was, I guess 16 or 17 years old, something like that. And this band leader he looked to battle music with our band, and Glen Gray and the Casaloma in Griffiths Stadium. I’ve never been so embarrassed in all my life. It was really, really depressing.
Glen Gray, he was a pretty popular group at the time. Right?
Oh, yeah, yeah. They were hot, and in tails, and all this shit. And we were just a chump, I guess about 13, about 12 or 13 piece band. Really embarrassing.
